text: dsh-kde-tint 是一个 DSH 网页端主题插件，会把 KDE Plasma 当前应用的配色带入 DSH 界面。服务端读取 kdeglobals 中的强调色和表面颜色，并在缺少配置时尝试读取颜色方案文件或使用默认值；浏览器端获取配色后生成浅色与深色主题，覆盖界面主题 token，也为少数局部 CSS 变量添加样式。它会为背景层、面板、按钮状态、边框和滚动条等界面元素着色，并保留文字和语义状态色。适合希望 DSH 网页界面与 KDE 桌面配色协调的用户；需要本机 KDE 配色文件，不需要额外 API 密钥。

dsh-kde-tint matches the DSH web interface to the active KDE palette. The server reads local KDE colors for the browser, which applies light and dark themes to surfaces, controls, borders, and scrollbars. It suits users who want DSH to match KDE and needs no API key.
让 DSH 网页界面的颜色跟着 KDE 当前配色走。
DSH 网页能不能用 Plasma 的系统强调色？
我想把 DSH 的面板、按钮和滚动条染成桌面主题的颜色。
dsh-kde-tint 的功能「同步 KDE 配色」：服务端读取当前 Plasma 配色，客户端在页面加载时获取结果并应用浅色和深色主题。背景层、控件、边框和滚动条会使用桌面强调色生成的配色。

dsh-kde-tint README · Background：The DSH web UI ships a neutral theme. On a KDE desktop the user already picks a color scheme. This plugin reads the **currently applied** colors and tints the DSH interface with them. The harness then matches the desktop.

dsh-kde-tint README · Background：The plugin has two halves. The host half (`lib/index.js`) reads the `Colors:*` sections that Plasma writes to `~/.config/kdeglobals`; on Material You / dynamic-color setups those sections carry the live palette, while the `.colors` file on disk can be stale. It serves the result as JSON from the profile web server. The browser half (`lib/client.js`) fetches the JSON and applies the tint through the `theme` service. The two halves talk over plain HTTP. A static client bundle has no host bridge, so HTTP is the correct channel.

dsh-kde-tint README · Background：The tint accent is `Colors:Selection.BackgroundNormal` (the applied selection color), not `General.AccentColor`, which often stays at an old manual value. `Colors:Window`, `Colors:View` and `Colors:Button` seed the surface ramp: the deepest canvas, the panel layer and the raised layer.

On systems without KDE configuration the plugin falls back to the active color-scheme file, then to defaults (accent `#386798`, scheme `MaterialYouDark`). It never blocks startup because of a missing config file.

dsh-kde-tint README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:iwinoid/dsh-kde-tint
```

Local development uses a link install instead:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-kde-tint
```

The package has no build step, so a git install needs no `allowBuilds` exception. The package ships `cordis.patch.yml` through `dsh.bundle.patch`, so the loader mounts it with no manual patch step. Restart `dsh web` after install.

Check the install:

```sh
dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep -A3 kde-tint
```
dsh-kde-tint README · Install：Then open the DSH web UI. Surfaces, controls, borders and scrollbars carry the applied KDE palette.

dsh-kde-tint README · Usage：The plugin needs no clicks. It loads with `immediately: true` and tints the UI on every page load. Uninstall (or disable) restores the stock theme. The token override is effect-scoped, so it unwinds with the plugin.

Upgrading from 0.2.x changes the host half as well, so restart `dsh web` once; after that a page refresh is enough.

dsh-kde-tint README · What gets tinted：The client builds a light and a dark palette from the applied scheme and overrides 57 DSH tokens. Surfaces mix 10–24% of the accent into the scheme's own base colors, so the UI keeps the desktop's depth instead of washing out. When the scheme is dark, `Colors:View` becomes the canvas, `Colors:Window` the sidebar, and `Colors:Button` the raised layers; a light scheme seeds the light palette the same way, and the other mode falls back to a neutral base plus accent.

dsh-kde-tint README · What gets tinted：| Group | Tokens |
| --- | --- |
| Surfaces | `bg-base`, `bg-layer-1/2/3`, `sidebar-fill`, `bg-overlay`, `bg-document-preview`, `bg-skeleton` |
| Message bubbles | `specific-bubble`, `specific-bubble-highlight` |
| Raised panels | `bg-module-platform`, `specific-input-major`, menu surfaces, `markdown-code-block` (+ banner, inline code, tag) |
| State fills | `interactive-bg-hover` / `-active` / `-hover-solid` |
| Neutral controls | `button-elevated-fill`, `button-floating-fill` / `-hover`, `button-ghost-active-fill` / `-border`, `button-contrast-fill`, `button-tool-bar-fill` / `-hover`, `specific-selector`, `switch-thumb` |
| Navigation | `specific-sidebar-nav-item-hover` / `-active` |
| Borders | `border-l1` … `border-l4`, `border-l2-darkmode-thin` |
| Scrollbars | `scrollbar-bg-l1` / `-l2`, `scrollbar-hover-l1` / `-l2` |
| Brand | `brand-primary` (raw selection accent), `button-primary-hover`, `button-primary-dimmed` |
| Toast / tooltip | `tooltip-bg`, `toast-bg` |
| Onboarding | `onboarding-card-fill`, `onboarding-secondary-fill`, `onboarding-checkbox-border` |

dsh-kde-tint README · What gets tinted：`--dsw-alias-label-primary-foreground` (the label on primary buttons) is picked from black or white by the accent's contrast, so it stays above 4.5:1 for any accent. Text tokens stay neutral (`#1a1d22` / `#e6e8eb` primary).

The plugin also defines three tokens that the installed DSH 0.2.1-rc.3 still references but never declares (`--dsw-alias-bg-layer-4`, `--dsw-alias-bg-l1`, `--dsw-alias-bg-l2`), because the missing variables otherwise leave some backgrounds unresolved.

dsh-kde-tint README · What gets tinted：A few DSH components hardcode their background in a component-local CSS variable, so token overrides cannot reach them. The client injects one small stylesheet that overrides these variables from the same palette (light and dark values follow `body[data-ds-dark-theme]`):

dsh-kde-tint README · What gets tinted：| Local variable | Component |
| --- | --- |
| `--dsw-hovercard-bg` | hover preview bubble (hardcoded `#2C2C2E`) |
| `--deliverable-fill` / `--deliverable-hover` | delivered-file cards in the transcript (hardcoded neutral 50/850) |
| `--changes-fill` / `--changes-hover` | changed-file card header (hardcoded neutral 50/850) |

dsh-kde-tint README · What is not tinted：Controls that already carry the DSH emphasis color keep it: `state-business-*` (focus borders, active underlines, references), `button-info-*` (the send button), links, the dock drop indicator, and semantic success/warning/error and diff colors. Shiki syntax colors and the terminal ANSI palette also stay as shipped.

dsh-kde-tint README · API：Debug endpoint on the profile web server:

```sh
curl http://localhost:<dsh-port>/api/kde-tint/kde-colors
```

`GET /api/kde-tint/kde-colors` returns `200` with JSON:

```json
{
  "accent": "#7c8fa3",
  "background": "#122236",
  "view": "#081421",

dsh-kde-tint README · API：`accent` is `Colors:Selection.BackgroundNormal` from the applied `kdeglobals` (the live scheme Material You writes), not `General.AccentColor`, which often stays at an old manual value. `background`, `view`, `button` and `tooltip` come from the matching `Colors:*` background entries and seed the surface ramp; they are `null` when the scheme does not define them. Values are normalized to `#rrggbb` (the sources may use `#hex` or `r,g,b`).

dsh-kde-tint README · API：`source` is `kdeglobals`, `scheme-file` (fallback to `~/.local/share/color-schemes` or `/usr/share/color-schemes`) or `defaults`. `scheme` is `General.ColorScheme`. When the read fails, the response still returns `200` with the default values plus an `error` string. Unknown routes return `404`.
